question: In my API spec, how do I mark which endpoints are visible to which user groups (like public vs internal)? Can one endpoint be visible to multiple groups? Where exactly do I add this in the spec file?
ground_truth: To mark an endpoint for specific audiences in OpenAPI, add the `x-fern-audiences` extension directly under the operation (e.g., under the `post:` key for a POST endpoint). The extension takes an array of audience values, allowing you to specify multiple audiences for a single endpoint. For example, to make the POST /users/sendEmail endpoint available to public and beta users but not internal: `paths: {/users/sendEmail: {post: {x-fern-audiences: [public, beta], operationId: send_email, ...}}}`. The endpoint will appear in SDK builds and documentation generated for any of the specified audiences. If you only specify `[public]`, it will only appear in public builds. This gives you fine-grained control over endpoint visibility across different consumer types without duplicating your API specification.

metadata.cited_context:
To mark an endpoint with a particular audience, add the `x-fern-audiences` extension to the relevant endpoint. In the example below, the `POST /users/sendEmail` endpoint is only available to public consumers:

```yaml title="openapi.yml" {{4-5}}
paths:
  /users/sendEmail:
    post:
      x-fern-audiences:
        - public
      operationId: send_email
```
